headline: Warm, dry Friday with highs in the mid to upper 70s, then light rain Saturday and cooler, mostly dry weather.
summary: High pressure aloft keeps western Washington dry and warm through Friday, with highs in the mid to upper 70s and fairly dry afternoon air (relative humidity in the upper 30s to low 40s percent). Tonight, winds from the east turn breezy, mostly in the Cascades and nearby foothills, where gusts will likely reach 25-30 mph, and they ease by Friday morning. Fog should be limited because the air is flowing from land toward the water, though isolated patchy fog is still possible in the south Sound and in fog-prone valleys. Winds return to blowing in from the ocean Friday afternoon. A weak front then crosses the area Saturday with light rain: a few hundredths of an inch for most lowlands and around a quarter inch in the Cascades. Parts of central Puget Sound could get even less because the moisture is weak and southwest winds may leave them in a rain shadow. Westerly winds pick up Saturday afternoon and evening in the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Admiralty Inlet. Sunday looks cool and mostly dry, with highs in the upper 50s and low 60s. A low-pressure system is expected Monday, but most computer models track it south of the area, so Monday should stay dry and cool, though this is less certain because not all models agree and the discussion's opening summary mentions rain early next week. Another weak front may bring isolated showers Wednesday into Thursday. No hazards are listed.
changes: The forecast was essentially unchanged. The evening discussion added detail: gusts of 25-30 mph in the Cascades and foothills tonight, and where isolated patchy fog is possible Friday morning.
